blocks.prompt: 13. If the lines \(2x + 3y - 7 = 0\), \(4x - y - 5 = 0\) and \(6x + ay - 9 = 0\) meet at a point, then find the value of \(a\).
blocks.explanation:
'Meet at a point' means the three lines are concurrent.
Theorem 3 gives an equation in \(a\).
Plan: determinant \(= 0\), solve for \(a\), check.
steps:
Given: \(2x + 3y - 7 = 0\), \(4x - y - 5 = 0\), \(6x + ay - 9 = 0\) are concurrent.
To find: \(a\).
Method: Theorem 3, set the determinant equal to zero and solve for \(a\).

Set up the determinant
\[\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 3 & -7 \\ 4 & -1 & -5 \\ 6 & a & -9 \end{vmatrix} = 0\]
Why: concurrent lines must give a zero determinant.

Expand along the first row
\[2(9 + 5a) - 3(-36 + 30) - 7(4a + 6) = 0\]
\[18 + 10a + 18 - 28a - 42 = 0\]
\[-6 - 18a = 0\]
Why: signs \(+, -, +\) along the first row; each \(2 \times 2\) minor is \(ps - qr\).

Solve
\[18a = -6\]
\[a = -\dfrac{1}{3}\]
Why: a linear equation in \(a\).

Check:
The first two lines meet at \(\left(\frac{11}{7}, \frac{9}{7}\right)\) (from \(y = 4x - 5\): \(14x - 22 = 0\)). In the third line:
\[6\left(\tfrac{11}{7}\right) - \tfrac{1}{3}\left(\tfrac{9}{7}\right) - 9 = \tfrac{66 - 3 - 63}{7} = 0\]
So the third line also passes through this point.
